claims.text: Section 102(d)(5) of the same Act is the residual authority every later covert-action directive is written under: the Agency is 'to perform such other functions and duties related to intelligence affecting the national security as the National Security Council may from time to time direct.'

claims.sourceText: National Security Act of 1947, Public Law 80-253, ch. 343, 61 Stat. 495, secs. 101(a), 102(a), 201(a), approved 26 July 1947, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/STATUTE-61/pdf/STATUTE-61-Pg495.pdf
claims.text: The statute approved on 26 July 1947 creates, in one instrument, the Council, the Agency and the military establishment: 'There is hereby established a council to be known as the National Security Council'; 'There is hereby established under the National Security Council a Central Intelligence Agency with a Director of Central Intelligence, who shall be the head thereof'; 'There is hereby established the National Military Establishment, and the Secretary of Defense shall be the head thereof.'

claims.text: On AREA52 - DEBRIEFED with Chris Ramsay, episode 20, 3 January 2025, at 0:12:27, Ramsay read aloud from John Lear's 1987 statement that 'several committed suicide, the most prominent of which was General James V. Forestall who jumped to his death from a 16th story hospital window. General Forestall's medical records are sealed to this day.' The document's rank is wrong: the statute creating the office he held requires a civilian appointee and bars any commissioned officer on active duty within the previous ten years.

claims.sourceText: National Security Act of 1947 sec. 102(d)(5), 61 Stat. 498, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/STATUTE-61/pdf/STATUTE-61-Pg495.pdf
claims.text: SECTION 102(d)(5) IS THE CLAUSE THAT MATTERS. It permits the Agency to perform such other functions and duties related to intelligence as the National Security Council may from time to time direct, and it is the authority expressly invoked by NSC 10/2 of 18 June 1948 and again by NSC 5412 of 15 March 1954. The United States covert-action programme rests on a residual clause in a reorganisation statute, not on a grant of authority written for it.

claims.sourceText: National Security Act of 1947 sec. 201(a), 61 Stat. 499, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/STATUTE-61/pdf/STATUTE-61-Pg495.pdf
claims.text: THE ACT DID NOT CREATE THE DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE, and the common claim that it did is wrong on the text. Section 201(a) reads 'There is hereby established the National Military Establishment, and the Secretary of Defense shall be the head thereof'. The renaming to Department of Defense came with the amendments of 10 August 1949, ch. 412, 63 Stat. 579.
